title: Guided Latent Spaces for Controllable Multi-Scenario Generation in Autonomous Driving (Student Abstract)

control_signal.value: Scenario type (cut-in, cut-out, cut-through, left or right), selected by choosing the value of one designated latent dimension.

control_mechanism.value: One latent dimension z_type encodes scenario class, with a class-conditional prior with per-class means and an auxiliary alignment loss pulling z_type to its class center.

base_model.value: Guided variational autoencoder over trajectories, with total loss of reconstruction, KL and alignment terms.

datasets.value: Real-world highway measurements (ego ECU signals plus surrounding-traffic sensors), about 44,600 trajectories across six safety-critical scenario types.

metrics.value: Validation MSE, classification error by an external classifier, PCA overlap of generated and real trajectories.

controllability_evidence.value: Each scenario type forms a distinct cluster in z0; an external classifier gives classification error between 0.00e+0 and 2.00e-2 across six scenario types.

stated_limitations.value: Generated samples show slightly looser clustering and partial overlap; cluster separation could improve with refined latent regularization. Future work: grounding latent space in physical parameters.

notes: Two-page student abstract; control is only over discrete scenario class, no continuous attribute control shown. No numbers for realism beyond MSE.
